meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Tong M, Jiang Y, Zhu R, Ding Z, Ma D et al.
articles.title: Artificial intelligence-powered renal pathology for glomerular disease classification: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 studies (39,536 validation units) evaluating AI models for glomerular disease classification. AI demonstrated high diagnostic performance across major subtypes, including membranous nephropathy (AUC 0.98), IgA nephropathy (AUC 0.96), and minimal change disease (AUC 1.00).

pico.outcome: Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, precision, accuracy, F1 score, AUC)

inclusion: Studies using pathology images and pathology diagnosis as the reference standard

appraisal.bottom_line: AI models achieve high diagnostic accuracy for classifying membranous nephropathy, IgA nephropathy, and minimal change disease, with performance metrics (AUC 0.96-1.00) suggesting potential superiority over senior pathologists in some datasets.
appraisal.relevance: AI-powered pathology could standardize glomerular disease diagnosis and assist pathologists, particularly in centers with limited subspecialty expertise.
appraisal.caveat: Most studies were retrospective and used 'validation sample units' rather than unique patients; substantial heterogeneity existed in imaging modalities and model architectures.

articles.authors: Zhou Y, Liao J, Huang W, Xiong Y
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of roxadustat for the treatment of renal anemia in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 19 randomized controlled trials involving 1,636 patients on peritoneal dialysis (PD) comparing roxadustat to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs). Roxadustat was associated with higher post-treatment hemoglobin levels (MD 7.30 g/L, 95% CI 5.43-9.16) and a lower reported adverse event rate (RR 0.45, 95% CI 0.27-0.74).

pico.population: Adults undergoing peritoneal dialysis with renal anemia
pico.outcome: Post-treatment hemoglobin levels and adverse event rates

inclusion: Randomized controlled studies comparing roxadustat-based to ESA-based regimens in adults receiving PD

appraisal.bottom_line: In patients on peritoneal dialysis, roxadustat significantly increased hemoglobin levels compared to ESAs (MD 7.30 g/L, 95% CI 5.43-9.16), though the certainty of evidence for most outcomes is low to very low.
appraisal.relevance: Provides PD-specific data for HIF-PHIs, confirming efficacy in a population often grouped with hemodialysis patients.
appraisal.caveat: Comparator ESA regimens were heterogeneous, and the lack of standardized reporting for hemoglobin target attainment and long-term safety limits definitive conclusions on clinical superiority.

articles.authors: Hu Y, Li H, Deng W, Diao S, Zeng L et al.
articles.title: Time-stratified prognostic factors for poor renal outcomes in childhood-onset lupus nephritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 47 studies identifying prognostic factors for poor renal outcomes in childhood-onset lupus nephritis (cLN). Key factors associated with progression included male sex, dialysis at onset, eGFR <60, hypertension, and renal non-remission at 6 or 12 months.
inclusion: Studies identifying prognostic factors independently associated with poor renal outcomes in cLN based on multivariable analyses

appraisal.bottom_line: Male sex, low baseline eGFR, hypertension, and failure to achieve renal remission within 12 months are robust independent predictors of poor renal outcomes in pediatric lupus nephritis.
appraisal.relevance: These factors allow for early risk stratification and potentially more aggressive management in high-risk pediatric patients.
appraisal.caveat: Nearly half of the included studies (23/47) were at high risk of bias, and the association of proteinuria with outcomes was not robust in sensitivity analyses.

articles.authors: Fountoulakis N, Pavlou P, Gnudi L, Maltese G, Panagiotou A et al.
articles.title: The effects of ursodeoxycholic acid on albuminuria in people with type 1 diabetes and diabetic kidney disease: a proof-of-concept study.
articles.summary: A single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of 31 participants with type 1 diabetes and DKD. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) 500 mg BID for 24 weeks did not significantly reduce the urine albumin excretion rate (UAER) compared to placebo (p=0.4).

pico.population: Patients with type 1 diabetes and DKD (UACR >3 mg/mmol, eGFR >=30, stable RAS blockade)
pico.intervention: Ursodeoxycholic acid (500 mg BID) for 24 weeks
pico.outcome: Change in urine albumin excretion rate (UAER)

appraisal.bottom_line: Ursodeoxycholic acid failed to reduce albuminuria in patients with type 1 diabetes and DKD over a 24-week treatment period (p=0.4).
appraisal.relevance: Despite promising preclinical data, UDCA does not appear to provide short-term renoprotection in this human population.
appraisal.caveat: The study was a small (n=31) proof-of-concept trial, which may be underpowered to detect modest effects or long-term benefits.

articles.authors: Snanoudj R, Marquant F, Renaudin K, Dubois V, Koenig A et al.
articles.title: Bortezomib in combination with standard-of-care for late active antibody-mediated rejection with de novo donor-specific antibodies after kidney transplantation: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.summary: A multicenter randomized trial of 60 kidney transplant recipients with late active antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and de novo donor-specific antibodies (dnDSA). Adding bortezomib to standard care did not improve the primary composite endpoint (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.61-2.34, p=0.59) and increased serious adverse events (76.7% vs 46.7%, p=0.017).

pico.population: Adult kidney transplant recipients with late active AMR and de novo DSA
pico.intervention: Bortezomib (two cycles) plus standard-of-care (steroids, PLEX, IVIG)
pico.outcome: Composite of >50% reduction in DSA MFI and biopsy stabilization/improvement at 12 months

appraisal.bottom_line: Bortezomib does not provide clinical or histologic benefit in late active AMR and is associated with a significantly higher burden of serious adverse events.
appraisal.relevance: This trial argues against the use of bortezomib for late AMR, highlighting the need for safer and more effective therapies in this difficult-to-treat population.
appraisal.caveat: The study was terminated early, enrolling only 60 of the planned 100 patients, which limits its statistical power.

articles.authors: Huang M, Zhang X, Kang Y, Lv H, Gao J et al.
articles.title: The Physical ACtivity Enhancement Scheme (PACES) improves physical activity level and well-being in persons with hemodialysis: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: A randomized controlled trial of 53 hemodialysis patients evaluating the Physical ACtivity Enhancement Scheme (PACES). The intervention group showed significant improvements in daily step counts and health-related quality of life (physical and mental components) compared to routine care.

pico.intervention: Physical ACtivity Enhancement Scheme (PACES) for 3 months
pico.outcome: Daily step count and well-being scores

appraisal.bottom_line: The PACES intervention effectively increases physical activity levels and improves well-being in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
appraisal.relevance: Structured physical activity programs can address the high burden of sedentary behavior and poor quality of life in the dialysis population.
appraisal.caveat: The study was small (n=53), single-center, and the trial was registered retrospectively; specific effect sizes for the primary outcome were not reported in the abstract.

articles.authors: Sulaiman AS, Nugroho P, Bestari MB, Afiatin A, Akil F et al.
articles.title: Sofosbuvir/Daclatasvir versus Grazoprevir/Elbasvir in Patients with Chronic Hepatitis C on Haemodialysis: A Multicentre, Single-Blind, Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: A multicenter, single-blind RCT of 120 treatment-naive HCV-infected hemodialysis patients comparing sofosbuvir/daclatasvir (SOF/DAC) to grazoprevir/elbasvir (GZR/EBR). Both regimens achieved 100% sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12).

pico.population: Treatment-naive, HCV-infected hemodialysis patients (fibrosis <F4 for randomization)

exclusion: Patients with cirrhosis (F4) were not randomized but assigned to SOF/DAC

appraisal.bottom_line: Sofosbuvir/daclatasvir is as effective as grazoprevir/elbasvir for treating hepatitis C in hemodialysis patients, with both achieving 100% SVR12.
appraisal.relevance: Supports the use of sofosbuvir-based therapy in dialysis, which is often more cost-effective and has broader pangenotypic activity.
appraisal.caveat: The study was single-blind, and the exclusion of cirrhotic patients from randomization limits the comparative safety and efficacy data in that specific subgroup.

articles.authors: Nair RG, Mavathur R, Manjunath NK, Manjunath J
articles.title: Efficacy of yoga and its probable mechanism of action on lifestyle-related chronic kidney disease: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.summary: A randomized clinical trial of 81 patients with stage 3-4 CKD evaluating a 12-week yoga intervention. The yoga group showed significant improvements in serum creatinine (MD -0.42 mg/dL, p=0.013), eGFR (MD 6.94 mL/min/1.73m2, p=0.030), and UACR (MD -464.2 mg/g, p=0.029).

pico.population: Patients with stage 3 and 4 CKD (diabetic or hypertensive etiology, aged 35-60)
pico.intervention: Yoga (12 weeks, 5 hours/week) plus usual care
pico.outcome: Kidney function parameters (creatinine, eGFR, UACR) and TGF-beta1

appraisal.bottom_line: A 12-week yoga program significantly improved eGFR and reduced albuminuria in patients with stage 3-4 CKD, potentially mediated by reductions in TGF-beta1 and oxidative stress.
appraisal.relevance: Yoga may serve as a low-cost, non-pharmacological adjunct to standard CKD care to slow disease progression.
appraisal.caveat: The reported eGFR improvement (nearly 7 mL/min/1.73m2) is remarkably high for a 12-week lifestyle intervention; the small sample size (n=81) necessitates larger confirmatory trials.
